label: words
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: fridge
Length: 30 s: 95-120 words in all, one sentence per beat (12 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 108 words in all, about 9 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 120 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- The refrigerant R-134a boils at about minus 26 degrees Celsius at normal air pressure
- Food safety agencies say a fridge should be at 4 degrees Celsius (40 F) or colder
- A fridge does not make cold; it moves heat from inside the box to the coils outside

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: food and a block of ice sit in the open box. actions: fridge show; fridge foodIn (on "food"); fridge iceIn (on "ice")
   idea: put food in a box with a block of ice and you already have a fridge
   cue words: "food", "ice"
2. problem
   on screen: the ice block shrinks and water drips. actions: fridge melt (on "melts"); drip start (on "melts")
   idea: the ice melts and drips onto the food
   cue words: "melts"
3. fix1
   on screen: a coil appears on the back wall and frosts over. actions: drip stop (on "So"); fridge iceInBack (on "So"); fridge meltBack (on "So"); fridge coilIn (on "coil"); fridge frost (on "frosts")
   idea: replace the ice with a coil of liquid that boils at minus 26 degrees, so the coil frosts over
   cue words: "So", "coil", "frosts", "26"
   its fact: The refrigerant R-134a boils at about minus 26 degrees Celsius at normal air pressure
4. problem2
   on screen: the frost melts off the coil and the thermometer climbs to 15. actions: fridge frostBack (on "boils"); temp up show; temp up count (on "boils"); auto_fx 1 start (on "melts")
   idea: once the liquid has boiled away the frost melts and the box warms up again
   cue words: "boils", "melts"
5. fix2
   on screen: a compressor appears, shakes, and liquid runs through the pipes. actions: temp up hide (on "So"); fridge compIn (on "compressor"); fridge pipesIn (on "compressor"); fridge run (on "squeezes"); fridge circulate (on "squeezes"); fridge frost (on "liquid"); auto_fx 1 stop
   idea: a compressor squeezes the gas back into a liquid and pumps it round, so the coil frosts again
   cue words: "So", "compressor", "squeezes", "liquid"
6. name
   on screen: a glowing outline traces the fridge. actions: outline show (on "refrigerator")
   idea: this box with a coil, a compressor and pipes is a refrigerator
   cue words: "refrigerator"
7. how
   on screen: the coils underneath glow hot and heat arrows flow out. actions: outline hide; fridge condIn (on "hot"); fridge hot (on "hot"); heat arrows show (on "heat")
   idea: squeezing makes the gas hot, so the coils underneath shed that heat into the kitchen
   cue words: "hot", "heat"
8. fact
   on screen: the thermometer counts down to 4. actions: heat arrows hide; temp down show; temp down count (on "holds")
   idea: inside it holds your food at 4 degrees, where germs grow slowly
   cue words: "holds", "4"
   its fact: Food safety agencies say a fridge should be at 4 degrees Celsius (40 F) or colder
9. myth
   on screen: white cold arrows point into the box, then vanish. actions: temp down hide; cold arrows show (on "cold"); cold arrows hide (on "not")
   idea: the cold you feel is not blown in
   cue words: "cold", "not"
10. mythFact
   on screen: orange arrows carry heat out of the box. actions: heat out show (on "heat"); heat arrows show (on "heat")
   idea: a fridge only moves heat out of the box
   cue words: "heat"
   its fact: A fridge does not make cold; it moves heat from inside the box to the coils outside
11. finish
   on screen: a glass door, shelves and a light pop on. actions: heat out hide (on "Add"); heat arrows hide (on "Add"); fridge doorOn (on "door"); fridge shelvesIn (on "shelves"); fridge lampOn (on "light")
   idea: a door, shelves and a light complete the fridge
   cue words: "Add", "door", "shelves", "light"
12. congrats
   on screen: the finished build, calm
   idea: calm end: the fridge hums with its door open and its light on
   cue words: (none)
